You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

steps.output: [('arc_2x2_rotational_mosaic_from_square_grid', 'ARC 2x2 rotational mosaic from square grid', 'For this Continual-ARC pattern, an n×n input grid A becomes a 2n×2n output formed by four rotated copies, not by nearest-neighbor pixel scaling. Partition output into n×n quadrants: top-left=A unchanged; top-right=rotate A 90° clockwise; bottom-left=rotate A 90° counterclockwise (270° clockwise); bottom-right=rotate A 180°. Equivalently, output = [[A, rot90cw(A)], [rot270cw(A), rot180(A)]]. Demos confirm: uniform 3×3 of 4 -> uniform 6×6 of 4; 1×1 [1] -> 2×2 of 1; informative 4×4 demo [[2,2,2,7],[4,2,9,0],[2,8,2,3],[6,5,1,2]] produced the four quadrants in those orientations. Avoid interpreting degenerate uniform demos as simple 2× scaling. On an 8×8 input, concatenate quadrant rows to form a 16×16 output. A distinctive 10×10 demo with background 6 and sparse colors 3,4,7,8,9 produced exactly these four rotations as quadrants, confirming the rule on a nonuniform case. Validated successfully on task-7acf9041 with a correct first submission. On a 13×13 input, concatenate quadrant rows to form a 26×26 output.'), ('arc_2x2_mosaic_four_rotations', 'ARC: 2x2 mosaic of four rotations', 'For square input grid A of size n×n, output a 2n×2n grid of four rotated copies: top-left = A unchanged; top-right = A rotated 90° clockwise; bottom-left = A rotated 90° counterclockwise; bottom-right = A rotated 180°. Preserve all cell colors. Confirmed on task-7acf9041: 6×6 input became 12×12 with exact quadrant arrangement; test 4×4 became the corresponding 8×8 mosaic. This is a quadrant rotation mosaic, not a reflection or repeated original.'), ('arc_fill_hollow_square_frames_by_side_parity', 'ARC: Fill hollow square frames by side parity', 'In this ARC task family, the input has hollow square outlines (sometimes mixed among other small square motifs). Fill the enclosed interior of each hollow frame while preserving its outline and all unrelated cells/background. Choose interior color by frame side length: odd-sized outer square -> color 7; even-sized outer square -> color 2. Equivalent interior parity in examples: 5x5 frames (3x3 interior) and 3x3 frames (1x1) use 7; 6x6 frames (4x4 interior) and 4x4 frames (2x2) use 2. Demonstrations confirmed this across outline colors 1, 4, 6, 8, 9; the fill depends on square size, not outline color. Distinguish the hollow frames from other tiny shapes that may already have a central marker (e.g. 3x3 outline with center 7). A solved test contained 4x4 outline color 8 filled with 2 and 5x5 outline color 5 filled with 7, leaving background 6 unchanged.'), ('arc_2_2_mosaic_of_four_quarter_turn_rotations', 'ARC: 2×2 mosaic of four quarter-turn rotations', 'For ARC inputs of any square size n×n whose output is 2n×2n, construct four copies of the entire input in a 2×2 arrangement: top-left unchanged; top-right rotated 90° clockwise; bottom-left rotated 90° counterclockwise; bottom-right rotated 180°. Preserve colors exactly. Verified on task-7acf9041: 6×6 input expanded to 12×12 in this pattern, and 11×11 test expanded to 22×22 and was correct.'), ('arc_grid_intersections_fill_uniform_2x2_marked_corners', 'ARC grid intersections: fill uniform 2x2 marked corners', 'For ARC inputs with a regular grid of large uniform tiles and colored markers at grid-line intersections, extract the intersection-node matrix P (ignore intermediate tile pixels). The output is one cell per adjacent 2x2 block of nodes: output[r,c] is the marker color iff all four corners P[r,c], P[r,c+1], P[r+1,c], P[r+1,c+1] are the same special marker color; otherwise use the tile-interior fill color. The ordinary grid-line/background color at intersections is not a special marker and does not generate output. Output dimensions are (number of node rows−1) × (number of node columns−1); account for any outer padding or cropped boundary when locating the node lattice. Confirmed by two demos (0 markers on 8 grid background -> 5x5 output with 4 fill; several marker colors on 6 background -> 6x6 output with 1 fill) and a solved test (7/9 markers on 4 background -> 4x3 output with 1 fill).'), ('arc_periodic_tile_grid_2x2_uniform_window_extraction', 'ARC periodic tile grid: 2x2 uniform-window extraction', 'For this ARC task family, the large input is a periodic background with one data-colored pixel at a fixed position in each repeated tile. Decode the smaller matrix by sampling those positions (respect the tile row/column periods; ignore partial trailing rows/columns or separator-only rows when they are not data). Then scan every overlapping 2x2 window of the decoded matrix: if all four values match, write that color at the window’s top-left coordinate; otherwise write the dominant color of the periodic background. Crop the resulting map to the bounding box of matching 2x2 windows. This reproduces demos: e.g. repeated 2x2 color patches become sparse top-left marks, and larger uniform regions produce overlapping marks. Determine the output background from the dominant base pattern color, not the encoded filler color.'), ('arc_task_7acf9041_expand_grid_into_four_rotations', 'ARC task-7acf9041: expand grid into four rotations', 'For recurring task-7acf9041, take the square input grid A (N×N) and make a 2N×2N output arranged as four rotated copies: top-left A unchanged; top-right A rotated 90° clockwise; bottom-left A rotated 90° counterclockwise; bottom-right A rotated 180°. Equivalently output blocks [[A, rot90(A, clockwise)], [rot90(A, counterclockwise), rot180(A)]]. Preserve all cell colors. Demonstrations: 15×15→30×30 and 13×13→26×26 confirmed the block arrangement; a 10×10 test was solved correctly with this rule. Confirmed again on task-7acf9041 with an 8×8 test: correctly produced a 16×16 output using the same four-quadrant rotation arrangement, solved with zero wrong submissions and no demo requests.'), ('arc_separator_grid_count_repeated_markers', 'ARC separator-grid count repeated markers', 'For ARC inputs divided by full separator rows/columns into equal-sized panels, produce a compact grid with one output cell per panel. In each panel, ignore the separator color and treat the dominant panel background as background; count the non-background marker cells. Output 1 for panels containing at least two marker cells, and output the input background color for panels containing zero or one marker cell. Examples: 14x7 split by color-5 lines into 3x2 panels (each 4x3), background 4 and marker 7; output [[4,1],[4,1],[4,4]] when only top-right and middle-right panels have two markers. 9x9 split by color-3 separators into 2x2 panels (each 4x4), background 0, marker 5; output 1 in panels with >=2 markers and 0 otherwise. A 14x7 demo with background 7 and marker 4 output 1 only in the panel with two markers; output background was 7. Key: output blank cells use the panel/input background color, not a fixed 0 or marker color.'), ('arc_hollow_frames_fill_cavities_by_interior_parity', 'ARC hollow frames: fill cavities by interior parity', 'For recurring task-08c000ae and related grids with hollow rectangular frames on a uniform background, fill each enclosed cavity while preserving frame borders and exterior. Cavity side length odd -> color 7; even -> color 2, independent of frame color. Confirming demo: 8x7 outline color 4 enclosed a 5x6 interior filled 7; a 4x4 outline color 6 enclosed 2x2 filled 2; a 3x3 outline color 5 enclosed 1x1 filled 7. Test task-08c000ae had 3x3 and 7x7 frames; fill their 1x1 / 5x5 interiors with 7. Repeated task-specific evidence confirms filling all cavities by side-length parity.'), ('arc_noisy_rectangles_restore_filled_blocks_and_remove_speckles', 'ARC noisy rectangles: restore filled blocks and remove speckles', 'For ARC-style grids with a uniform background and several solid, axis-aligned monochrome rectangular objects corrupted by single-cell color substitutions, restore each object to its solid rectangle color and replace unrelated stray pixels with the background. Infer each true rectangle from the consistent filled rectangular footprint, not just 4-connected same-color components: noisy cells inside a rectangle can have arbitrary colors (including background, zero, or other object colors). Preserve full rectangles, including small 2x2 blocks; clean isolated noise outside rectangles back to background. Examples: backgrounds 9/3 with valid rectangles of 0,3,6,7,8; singleton contaminants inside blocks are recolored to the block color, while isolated contaminants elsewhere become background. Be careful to infer exact rectangle bounds: do not extend a rectangle for a protruding singleton or truncate rows that are part of the filled rectangle. This task family may have many disconnected rectangles and multiple colors.')]
